title: Getting Started with stHawkesTools
text: Hawkes model combines log-linear background rate (exogenous events) self-excitation governed triggering kernel. Parameters supplied named list entries background rate, triggering rate, parameters spatial temporal kernels. background rate list can include regression coefficients spatial covariates present; use intercept coefficient center covariate constructed . intercept corresponds baseline log-intensity roughly exp(−6.5)≈0.0015\exp(-6.5) \approx 0.0015 events per unit area per unit time. Adding three times center covariate increases intensity towards middle region, triggering rate controls many offspring event tends generate.
code: true_params <- list(   background_rate = list(intercept = -6, center = 5),   triggering_rate = 0.5,   spatial   = list(mean = 0, sd = 0.45),   temporal  = list(rate = 1.5) ) true_params #> $background_rate #> $background_rate$intercept #> [1] -6 #>  #> $background_rate$center #> [1] 5 #>  #>  #> $triggering_rate #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $spatial #> $spatial$mean #> [1] 0 #>  #> $spatial$sd #> [1] 0.45 #>  #>  #> $temporal #> $temporal$rate #> [1] 1.5

title: Getting Started with stHawkesTools
text: Parameter estimation uses expectation–maximisation (EM) algorithm implemented hawkes_mle(). function requires initial values format rHawkes(). Providing reasonable starting values helps algorithm converge quickly; perturb true parameters slightly. returned hawkes_fit object stores parameter estimates, fitted residuals original hawkes data. standard summary() method reports point estimates alongside Wald standard errors confidence intervals derived observed information matrix.
code: initial_values <- list(   background_rate = list(intercept = -6, center = 2.5),   triggering_rate = 0.5,   spatial   = list(mean = 0, sd = 0.5),   temporal  = list(rate = 1.8) )  est <- hawkes_mle(   hawkes,   inits = initial_values,   boundary = 0.5,   max_iters = 200 )  est #> Triggering Parameter Estimates: #> Background Rate (β):    #>     intercept: -6.696 #>     center: 5.813 #>  Triggering Rate (θ):   0.419 #>  #> Spatial Triggering Parameter Estimates: #>     mean: 0 #>     sd: 0.477 #> Temporal Triggering Parameter Estimates: #>     rate: 0.897 summary(est) #> Asymptotic confidence inervals are known to undercover. Consider bootstrap methods. #> Number of events: 153 #>  #> Residuals: #>      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max  #> 0.001687 0.292040 0.647415 1.314780 5.819229  #>  #> Coefficients: #>                            Estimate Std. Error     2.5%  97.5% #> Background Rate: Center     5.81273    0.46159  4.90804  6.717 #> Background Rate: Intercept -6.69587    0.43128 -7.54117 -5.851 #> Triggering Rate             0.41918    0.08974  0.24330  0.595 #> Spatial: Mean               0.00000    0.07096 -0.13908  0.139 #> Spatial: Sd                 0.47727    0.06184  0.35606  0.598 #> Temporal: Rate              0.89743    0.32869  0.25322  1.542 #>  #> Confidence level used: 95.0%

what: Uncertainty assessment with the cluster bootstrap
title: Getting Started with stHawkesTools
text: Spatial-temporal clustering can produce highly skewed sampling distributions MLEs. cluster bootstrap repeatedly resamples whole estimated clusters re-estimates model, capturing dependence structure. cluster_bootstrap() function requires fitted hawkes object, corresponding hawkes_fit, number bootstrap replications B. row contains bootstrap median, percentile-based interval, estimated standard deviation, proportion bootstrap fits failed converge (). Larger B yields smoother estimates cost additional computation; parallel processing available setting parallel = TRUE configuring future plan.
code: boot_results <- cluster_bootstrap(   hawkes = hawkes,   est = est,   B = 3,   alpha = 0.05,   boundary = 0.5,   max_iters = 200 )  boot_results #> # A tibble: 6 × 8 #>   parameter_type  parameter       boot_est_median  lower  upper width     sd #>   <chr>           <chr>                     <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1 background_rate center                    5.18   5.05   6.04  0.991 0.565  #> 2 background_rate intercept                -6.05  -6.85  -5.95  0.895 0.518  #> 3 spatial         mean                      0      0      0     0     0      #> 4 spatial         sd                        0.500  0.405  0.565 0.160 0.0845 #> 5 temporal        rate                      0.843  0.501  1.11  0.608 0.321  #> 6 triggering_rate triggering_rate           0.395  0.338  0.536 0.198 0.107  #> # ℹ 1 more variable: percent_failed <dbl>

text: stHawkesTools provides utilities simulating, fitting, diagnosing general spatio-temporal Hawkes processes. package wraps estimation routines based EM algorithm together simulation helpers, visualization utilities, bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification support end--end analysis workflows.

title: stHawkesTools: Provide Tools for Bootstrapping General Spatio-Temporal Hawkes Processes — stHawkesTools-package
text: stHawkesTools R package simulating, estimating, analyzing spatio-temporal Hawkes processes. supports flexible triggering kernels beyond implemented existing packages like ETAS, provides simulation tools tailored spatio-temporal settings. Parameter estimation performed using EM algorithm maximum likelihood inference. package also offers confidence intervals based asymptotic theory range bootstrap methods. Additional utilities included support diagnostics model-based analysis spatio-temporal point process data.

code: spatial_region <- create_rectangular_sf(0, 10, 0, 10)  params <- list(   background_rate = list(intercept = -4),   triggering_rate = 0.75,   spatial = list(mean = 0, sd = 0.75),   temporal = list(rate = 2) ) hawkes <- rHawkes(params, time_window = c(0, 50), spatial_region = spatial_region) est <- hawkes_mle(hawkes, inits = params) subsample(hawkes, est, 5, 25, alpha = 0.05) #> # A tibble: 5 × 8 #>   parameter_type  parameter       subsamp_est_median  lower  upper  width     sd #>   <chr>           <chr>                        <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1 background_rate intercept                   -3.38  -3.78  -3.34  0.436  0.219  #> 2 spatial         mean                         0      0      0     0      0      #> 3 spatial         sd                           0.684  0.672  0.837 0.165  0.0754 #> 4 temporal        rate                         2.59   2.48   2.74  0.264  0.107  #> 5 triggering_rate triggering_rate              0.647  0.629  0.658 0.0291 0.0123 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: percent_failed <dbl>

title: Compute time-scaled residuals — time_scaled_residuals
code: spatial_region <- create_rectangular_sf(0, 10, 0, 10)  params <- list(   background_rate = list(intercept = -4),   triggering_rate = 0.5,   spatial = list(mean = 0, sd = 0.1),   temporal = list(rate = 2) ) hawkes <- rHawkes(params, time_window = c(0, 100), spatial_region = spatial_region) est <- hawkes_mle(hawkes, inits = params) residuals <- time_scaled_residuals(hawkes, est)  curve(   dexp(x, rate = 1),   from = 0,   to = 10,   lwd = 2,   xlab = "Residual",   ylab = "Density",   main = "Residual vs Exponential(1)" ) lines(density(residuals, from = 0), col = "red")
